summary: On node1, cron access was restricted to root and opsadmin only via /etc/cron.allow (Vixie cron allow-list mechanism). The opsadmin user was created since it did not previously exist. Enforcement was verified before and after a full node restart: root and opsadmin can create crontabs, while other users (tested with testdeny and nobody) are denied with "cannot use this program (crontab)". The restart evidence protocol was completed: boot_id changed from bdd5de93-e94e-4d33-8384-6a01c51a3d49 to ec37444a-5558-4aff-a094-c4b4ff85cf49, proving an actual reboot occurred, and /etc/cron.allow, the cron service, and enforcement behavior were all confirmed intact post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected existing cron config on node1: no /etc/cron.allow or /etc/cron.deny existed, cron service was active
Created missing opsadmin user (uid 1000) via useradd -m -s /bin/bash
Created /etc/cron.allow containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin' (mode 644), ensured no /etc/cron.deny exists
Verified enforcement: created a temporary testdeny user, confirmed crontab access was denied for it
Verified root and opsadmin can successfully install and list crontabs
Cleaned up test crontabs for root/opsadmin and removed temporary test users (testdeny, testuser2)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline (cron.allow contents, cron service active/enabled)
Issued a backgrounded systemctl reboot on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned, confirming a changed boot_id as proof of restart
Re-verified post-restart: /etc/cron.allow persisted, cron service active/enabled, opsadmin user intact, and root/opsadmin allowed while an arbitrary user (nobody) was denied crontab access

evidence.requirement: Baseline: current cron config, users, and service state before changes
evidence.summary: Confirmed no cron.allow/cron.deny existed, cron service active, opsadmin user absent, root present

evidence.requirement: Restrict cron scheduling to root and opsadmin only
evidence.summary: Created /etc/cron.allow with exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin', removed any cron.deny

evidence.requirement: Prove non-listed users are denied cron scheduling
evidence.summary: testdeny user's crontab install attempt failed with 'cannot use this program (crontab)', exit=1

evidence.requirement: Prove root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: Both root and opsadmin successfully installed and listed a crontab entry, exit=0
Removed test crontabs, deleted testdeny and testuser2 accounts

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before restart (boot identity + cron config/service state)
evidence.summary: cron.allow contains root/opsadmin, no cron.deny, cron service active/enabled, pre-restart boot_id bdd5de93-e94e-4d33-8384-6a01c51a3d49 captured
Backgrounded systemctl reboot command returned 'reboot scheduled' before node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node restart causes disconnection then reconnection with changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Connection reset confirms node down; subsequent poll succeeded with new boot_id ec37444a-5558-4aff-a094-c4b4ff85cf49, differing from pre-restart value, proving an actual reboot

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron access control and enforcement
evidence.summary: After restart: /etc/cron.allow still contains root/opsadmin, no cron.deny, cron service active/enabled, opsadmin user intact, root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs, and user 'nobody' is denied access
